title: How Long Would You Last on the Floor of the Mariana Trench? Pt.1 #shorts
description_hook: You wake up on the floor of the Mariana Trench, 10,935 meters down, with no submarine. The clock starts now.

beats.say: Gumi here. You just woke up on the floor of the Mariana Trench. 10,935 meters down. No submarine.
beats.img: a lone human silhouette standing on the dark silty floor of the deepest ocean trench, a faint beam of light from far above, crushing darkness all around

beats.say: It is pitch black. Sunlight gave up at 1,000 meters. The water is 2.4 degrees Celsius.
beats.img: total darkness of the deep sea with a few faint bioluminescent specks, the last trace of light fading far overhead

beats.say: Then the water hits. More than 16,000 PSI. That's about 8 tons on every square inch.
beats.img: extreme close-up of heavy deep ocean water pressing in, tiny particles of marine snow drifting through a narrow beam of light

beats.say: Over 1,000 times the pressure at the surface. The air in your lungs is squeezed to a thousandth of its size.
beats.img: a glowing x-ray style outline of human lungs collapsing under immense pressure, deep blue darkness around it

gumi.say: Gumi's odds: zero. A NOAA microphone lasted 23 days down here. You won't.
